slice: RFC 8288-aware Link header parsing for retained workflow pagination evidence

github_pagination_documentation.finding: GitHub directs clients to follow the URL associated with rel=next until no next link remains.

rfc_8288.finding: Link is a structured HTTP field whose comma separators must be interpreted outside URI references and quoted parameter values.

prior_gap: The committed validator used link.split(',') and a single strict regular expression. That can misparse a valid URI reference or quoted parameter containing a comma and did not distinguish malformed Link syntax from an absent next relation.
implementation: Added state-aware Link value splitting across URI-reference and quoted-string boundaries.
Added relation-token parsing with case-insensitive parameter names.
Rejected malformed syntax and conflicting duplicate rel=next targets fail-closed.
Preserved exact next-URL continuity validation and the existing public nextUrlFromLink interface.

covered: relation token list and case-insensitive REL parameter

uncertainty: The complete repository test suite was not executed in an authenticated checkout.
No live private-repository pagination response was captured in this slice.
The parser intentionally supports the subset needed for GitHub pagination evidence rather than claiming complete RFC 8288 implementation.
falsification_route: Provide a valid GitHub Link header that the parser rejects.
Provide malformed or ambiguous Link syntax that the parser accepts as a complete chain.
Demonstrate a divergence between the parser's next target and GitHub's documented rel=next target on retained raw response evidence.
handoff: Run the complete committed Node test file, then exercise both authenticated enumeration clients against one exact commit and retain raw Link headers for parser-versus-provider comparison.
